source: Gong, Wan, Wang (2024) Working Memory Capacity of ChatGPT: An Empirical Study
finding: ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo) was run on verbal and spatial n-back tasks. Its d-prime stays above 1 up to about 3-back in the verbal task, and the authors call this similar to humans.
numbers: 50 blocks per n (n=1,2,3), 24 trials per block (8 match, 16 non-match), so 1,200 trials per n per condition. Verbal base d'>1 test: 1-back p=8.9e-16, 2-back p=1.9e-5, 3-back p=0.048 (r=0.27, marginal).
quote: Typical human performance drops significantly when n=3.
limits: Human comparison is only a plot of Jaeggi 2010 data, no numbers in text. 'Strikingly similar' is qualitative. Hit and false-alarm values appear only in figures.
agent_relevance: Do not read an n-back drop in a model as a human-like capacity. Treat it as a probe of the prompt, not of a trainable store.

source: Gong, Wan, Wang (2024) Working Memory Capacity of ChatGPT: An Empirical Study (spatial and model comparison)
finding: In the spatial task ChatGPT is not above threshold at 2-back or 3-back in the 3x3 base grid. Bigger grids help. GPT-4 beats GPT-3.5 and the seven open models.
numbers: Spatial base: 1-back p=1.9e-9, 2-back p=0.94, 3-back p=0.97. Grid 7x7 stays above d'=1 at 2-back (p=1.4e-6); 5x5 (p=0.10) and 4x4 (p=0.29) do not. Model test vs d'=1: GPT-4 above at 1,2,3-back (p=9.3e-10 each); GPT-3.5 at 1/2/3-back p=9.3e-10, 0.007, 0.035; the other seven models (Bloomz, ChatGLM, Vicuna) not significantly different from d'=1.
limits: Only GPT-4 on the base verbal task, 30 blocks per model. A falling false-alarm trend with n in the spatial task is rarely seen in humans.
agent_relevance: Capacity in a model scales with model quality, not with practice on the task. This is the opposite of the human claim that n-back practice raises Gf.

source: Gong, Wan, Wang (2024) Working Memory Capacity of ChatGPT: An Empirical Study (prompt manipulations)
finding: Noise symbols removed the n effect. Feedback and chain-of-thought helped at low n only. No few-shot or task-switch test was run.
numbers: Verbal noise: Kruskal-Wallis H=3.92, p=0.14, no level above d'=1. Verbal feedback above threshold at 1-back only (2-back p=0.25, 3-back p=0.68). Verbal CoT above threshold at 1- and 2-back (2-back p=1.5e-8), not at 3-back (p=0.22). Spatial CoT: no effect at 2- or 3-back.
limits: Temperature value in the paper looks like a typo. Per-trial feedback is the only practice-like element and it did not lift the 2-back spatial result.
agent_relevance: Within-session feedback does not buy capacity. A scaffold (CoT) helps one load level, then the limit returns. Same shape as human training: gains stop at the trained task.

source: Gong and Zhang (2024) Self-Attention Limits Working Memory Capacity of Transformer-Based Models
finding: Small decoder-only transformers were trained from scratch on n-back. Accuracy falls as N rises, and attention entropy rises with N. The authors propose that dispersed attention causes the limit.
numbers: 1 layer, 1 head, no FFN or layer norm. 50 models per N, 10 epochs, 24 letters, 8 matches, N=1..6, 800 train and 200 test sequences per N. Kruskal-Wallis H=38.517, p<.001, eps2=0.248. 1 vs 2: U=1825, r=-0.46; 1 vs 3: U=2096, r=-0.68; 2 vs 3: U=1665, p=.0128, r=-0.33. Larger models mostly above 95% but still dip slightly with N.
quote: the total entropy of the attention score matrix increases as N increases
limits: Tiny toy models. Per-N accuracy and entropy values only in figures. Correlations given without coefficients. Link to human capacity is by analogy.
agent_relevance: The limit appears even when the model is trained directly on the task. Training on the paradigm did not remove the load effect, which fits the human null result.

source: Hu and Lewis (2025) Do Language Models Understand the Cognitive Tasks Given to Them? Investigations with the N-Back Paradigm
finding: Weak models fail 2-back and 3-back because they do the wrong task (they answer as if it were 1-back). This challenges the claim of a human-like capacity limit.
quote: suggesting that its poor performance stems from an inability to understand the task, rather than any memory limitation.
limits: Eight models only. Intro and Section 4.5 give the same figures to different conditions (noted inconsistency). No exact drift rates.
agent_relevance: Check that a failure is a memory failure and not task misreading before building a fix. Same lesson as the human literature on strategy versus capacity.

source: Hu and Lewis (2025) (instruction, demo and curriculum effects)
finding: Demonstrations fix the mid-tier model but not the weakest. An in-context curriculum raised long n-back for Llama 3.1 70B. Reciting the last n letters raised even weak models.
numbers: Llama3.1-70B at n=8/9/10: retrieval 79.83/80.17/71.67% and task accuracy 90.08/90.08/84.75% with curriculum, versus retrieval 75.25/66.08/57.1% and task 83.33/78.25/71.92% without. Interactive demo, 3-back: Llama70B 0.62 (-.31), Gemma27B 0.31 (-.05). Qwen1.5-14B never got two correct in 10 demo sequences. Gemma27B 2-back: demos flip the log-prob ranking to the correct m; instructions alone do not.
limits: Reciting the n most recent letters changes the task (a rehearsal aid), so authors call it non-comparable. Single run per condition.
agent_relevance: An external rehearsal step (write the last n items) lifts capacity at once. This is the scaffold route, and it works where practice does not. Fits schema operators that restate state.

source: Zhang, Jian, Ouyang, Vosoughi (2024) Working Memory Identifies Reasoning Limits in Language Models
finding: n-back d-prime was measured across model sizes (text-ada-001 to GPT-4, plus LLaMA family). Scale helps, but models still struggle under complex load. Advanced prompts help big models and hurt small ones.
numbers: Dataset from Gong 2024; grids 4x4, 5x5, 7x7. On BIG-Bench Hard world-knowledge tasks, GPT-3.5 answer-only 57.1% vs 62.93% mean of five prompt methods (CoT, AutoCoT, SC-CoT, PS, ToT); GPT-4 answer-only 74.8%. A bigger spatial grid raised d' for models. Alignment seen as a cost ('alignment tax') for GPT-3.5.
limits: Authors admit n-back does not measure working memory fully (cites Jaeggi 2010 on weak correlation with complex span), no latency, no practice effect in static weights. Numeric d' tables only for the LLaMA family; most claims are heuristic.
agent_relevance: Prompt gains depend on model size. Do not ship one scaffold to every model tier. Test each tier.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) Working Memory Identifies Reasoning Limits (prompt interventions from human strategies)
finding: Strategies borrowed from human n-back participants (rehearsal, arousal-like focus, code structure) were turned into prompt tweaks and lifted task accuracy.
numbers: Small model text-ada-001 with 'after thinking carefully' answer prompt: 25.4% on Tracking Shuffled Objects (+15.8 points over standard CoT). text-davinci-002 with code-style logic: 96.4% (+4.8). Rehearsal prompt on Object Counting: 94.8% (+18). Trigger phrase 'so before that' on Temporal Sequence: GPT-3.5 96% (+32.8).
limits: Per-task prompt hand-tuning, single task each, no held-out transfer test. Interview of human participants is small and described in an appendix.
agent_relevance: Strategy cues (rehearse, refocus, chunk with code) transfer from human strategy talk into prompts. This is the strategy-teaching result of the human literature, not capacity training.

source: Huang, Sun, Wang, Dredze (2025) Language Models Do Not Have Human-Like Working Memory
finding: Three hidden-state tasks (guess a number silently, yes/no deduction, math magic) show models cannot keep a silent value across turns. Chain of thought fixes only Math Magic, by writing the steps out.
numbers: Number Guessing (ideal sum 1.0): seven models scored 0, LLaMA-3.1-405B 1.195, GPT-4o-0806 1.085, DeepSeek-R1 0.640. Yes-No Deduction: GPT-4o-mini 200/200 failures, GPT-4o 173/200. Math Magic no-CoT: 0-26% (LLaMA-405B 26.0%); with CoT or reasoning: o3-mini 96.7%, QwQ-32B 90.0%, DeepSeek-R1 100%, GPT-4o-0806 20.7%. CoT did not improve Number Guessing.
quote: LLMs do not exhibit behavior indicative of a functional working memory.
limits: No human baseline measured. 150 trials per model on Math Magic, 200 on Yes-No. Seven over-represented in answers (66.7% for o1-mini).
agent_relevance: Do not rely on hidden state. Any value the agent must keep has to be written into the visible context. Supports guardrail style rules about externalising state.

source: Wang and Sun (2025) Unable to Forget: Proactive Interference Reveals Working Memory Limits in LLMs Beyond Context Length
finding: Streaming related key-value updates and asking for the final value shows log-linear decay in retrieval. Errors are old values. Model size predicts resistance; context length does not.
numbers: 46 keys, 3 to 400 updates per key. llama4-maverick near 100% at 2 tracked keys, below 5% at 46. Value length: below 40% at 10 words, below 5% at 40 words for every model. Size predicts Interference Endurance Score (t=3.03, p=0.005, N=30 open models); context length does not (t=-0.144, p=0.886); R2=0.261.
limits: No human data collected. Slope given only as 'approximately log-linear'. Human comparison is a conceptual argument (gating, directed forgetting).
agent_relevance: Capacity is about interference, not storage size. Long context is not a fix. The agent should drop stale state, not just append.

source: Wang and Sun (2025) Unable to Forget (mitigation prompts)
finding: Telling the model to forget did not work. A fake question-answer turn that closes the earlier input helped a lot.
numbers: 'Forget' instruction: under 10 percentage points at 100 updates, hurt gpt-4.1-mini. Forward-focus, soft reset, relevance meta-prompt: little or none. Mock QA reset: Gemini Flash 2.0 at 150 updates matched its baseline at 30-45 updates.
limits: Accuracy still declines with more updates. Tested on one retrieval format.
agent_relevance: A structural reset (new turn, clean state summary) beats an instruction to forget. Good for a state-reset operator in a scaffold.

source: Wang and Sun (2025) Unable to Forget (human contrast)
finding: Authors contrast human recall, which plateaus under interference, with LLM accuracy that keeps falling. They say humans use gating and directed forgetting that LLMs lack.
numbers: Human numbers not given in the paper. Within 128k-131k context, size and IES Spearman rho2=0.673 (p=0.0016).
limits: A conceptual contrast, not measured by the authors. Weakens any 'LLM equals human WM' reading.
agent_relevance: The gap is a missing mechanism (unbinding), which a scaffold can supply, so scaffold is a better bet than training here.

source: Xie et al. (2025/2026) Play to Generalize: Learning to Reason Through Game Play (ViGaL)
finding: RL of Qwen2.5-VL-7B on Snake and a Rotation task, with no math data, raised multimodal math scores. This is far transfer from a game that worked in a model.
numbers: Base vs Snake+Rotation: Math avg 47.7 to 50.6; MathVista 68.0 to 71.9; MathVerse 49.0 to 52.4; MMMU val 54.3 to 58.0; VSI-Bench 36.7 to 38.7; general visual 72.4 to 72.2 (kept). MM-Eureka (math-trained) math avg 50.1. Ablation: random reward labels 49.4 vs 62.3 for real reward; SFT 47.2 vs RL 62.3.
limits: Gains are a few points. Text cites 63.1 overall where the table shows 64.7. Rotation lowers Expression accuracy. Pass@k at large k favours the base model.
agent_relevance: Models can show far transfer from narrow task training, unlike humans on n-back. But this needs RL with a verifiable reward and weight updates, which the scaffold agent will not do.

source: SPIRAL: Self-Play on Zero-Sum Games Incentivizes Reasoning via Multi-Agent Multi-Turn RL (ICLR 2026)
finding: Self-play on TicTacToe, Kuhn Poker and Simple Negotiation raised math and general reasoning on held-out benchmarks. The gain beats SFT on game data.
numbers: 8-benchmark average, base to SPIRAL-Multi: Qwen3-4B 34.0 to 44.5 (+10.5; SFT 39.7); Qwen3-8B 39.5 to 49.6; Octothinker-8B 25.8 to 33.8; Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 23.9 to 25.9 (+2.0); DS-R1-Distill-7B 60.4 to 61.8 (+1.4). Qwen3-4B AIME24 +10.1, AMC-23 +19.2, MMLU-Pro +11.3. 400 steps, 128 samples per step.
limits: Only Qwen3-4B was run with 3 seeds (44.5 +/- 0.5 vs SFT 39.6 +/- 0.4). Abstract says four models but table has five. Gain shrinks for strong or instruct models.
agent_relevance: Transfer shrinks for models that already reason well. Weight training is out of scope for a prompt-only scaffold.

source: SPIRAL (ablations and failure case)
finding: Which game is used matters, and a bad opponent removes the gain. Mixed games beat any single game.
numbers: Qwen3-4B average: TicTacToe only 41.3, Kuhn Poker only 43.4, Simple Negotiation only 40.0, all three 44.5. Trained against fixed Mistral-Small-3 opponent: 29.6, below the 34.0 base.
limits: Appendix numbers do not match Table 1 in places (DS-Distill 59.7 to 61.7 vs 60.4 to 61.8). Single runs for most cells.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition for model training transfer: it depends on task mix and curriculum. Human WM training has the same issue of trained-task specificity.

source: Reasoning Gym: Reasoning Environments for RL with Verifiable Rewards
finding: GRPO on procedural puzzle domains with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct transfers to other domains and to MATH. Some domains do not transfer at all.
numbers: Cross-domain Acc@3: Algebra 23.83 to 52.89 (+29.1, trained on Algorithmic); Geometry 0.83 to 23.17; Cognition 11.62 to 24.94 (+13.3, from Logic). ARC 6.49: no transfer improved it (-2.3). External: MATH 48.5 to 58.2 (+9.7); GSM8K 76.2 to 76.7 (+0.5, noise); BBH 8.68 to 16.34.
limits: Only 50 problems per eval set. RG-Algorithmic lowered MMLU-Pro Math by 0.74. Weak coverage of knowledge-heavy or free-text domains.
agent_relevance: Transfer is real but selective and mostly near-domain (algebra, arithmetic, logic). Far transfer to ARC fails, matching the honest ARC control in this project.

source: Gandhi et al. (2025) Cognitive Behaviors that Enable Self-Improving Reasoners
finding: Under the same RL on Countdown, Qwen-2.5-3B improves far more than Llama-3.2-3B. Priming Llama with four reasoning behaviors (verification, backtracking, subgoals, backward chaining) closes the gap.
numbers: Countdown after RL: Qwen-2.5-3B about 60%, Llama-3.2-3B about 30%. Empty-CoT control about 30-35%. Qwen MATH 38% to 50% with the authors' format. On GPQA both Llama pretraining variants scored about 12%, no difference.
quote: the presence of reasoning behaviors, rather than correctness of answers, proves to be the critical factor
limits: Exact primed score not in text; figure-only. Gains shown on Countdown, with limited generalisation test (GPQA flat).
agent_relevance: Training transfer depends on a prior skill base (behaviours already present). Teach behaviours, not raw task practice. Backward chaining and verification match scaffold operators.

source: Li et al. (2024) Chain of Thought Empowers Transformers to Solve Inherently Serial Problems
finding: Theory and tests show CoT acts as serial computation, letting a shallow transformer solve problems it cannot in one pass. It is not a memory store.
numbers: Constant-depth, constant-precision transformers without CoT sit in AC0. With T CoT steps they can solve any problem a boolean circuit of size T solves. Gains on permutation composition, iterated squaring, circuit value; largest for low depth.
quote: any problem solvable by boolean circuits of size T
limits: Abstract only was read. Expressiveness bounds, not what training finds.
agent_relevance: Written steps are the machine's working memory and compute. Scaffold design should budget steps for this, not hope for a bigger hidden store.

source: Hsieh et al. (2024) RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
finding: Models claim 32K or more context, but only half hold up at 32K on harder synthetic tasks.
numbers: 17 long-context models, 13 tasks. All claim context of at least 32K tokens; only about half keep satisfactory performance at 32K. Yi-34B claims 200K but shows large room for improvement.
limits: Abstract only was read.
agent_relevance: Nominal window is not working capacity. Keep agent context short and structured.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
finding: An agent loop with tiered memory (main context and external store) with interrupts, to give the model more usable memory than its window.
numbers: Tested on document analysis beyond the window and multi-session chat. No numbers in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only. Quantitative gains not read here.
agent_relevance: A production example of an external working-memory manager inside an agent loop. It is a scaffold, not a trained capacity.

source: Taatgen (2013) The nature and transfer of cognitive skills (PRIMs, ACT-R)
finding: A cognitive architecture explains transfer as shared primitive production elements, a syntactic account. The page says task-switching training improves working memory capacity tests and cuts Stroop interference.
numbers: The project page gives no effect sizes or sample sizes.
quote: PRIMs can explain transfer in Anderson and Singley's text editor study
limits: Project page summary only, outdated. Paper not opened. Claim relies on shared building blocks, not capacity growth.
agent_relevance: A principled view: transfer needs shared procedure, not general capacity. Supports teaching procedures (operators) over drilling memory.

source: Schmidt et al. (2023) Representational Tenets for Memory Athletics
finding: A note from memory-champion practice. Expert memory uses the method of loci with chunked, rehearsed material. Fixed-circuit expertise is rigid in transfer, and flexible one-shot learning is not of fixed capacity.
numbers: No experiments. Describes preparation of one Grandmaster co-author and proposes experiments.
quote: working memory mechanisms affording one-shot learning are thus not of a fixed capacity
limits: Subjective report of a single athlete. Not an LLM study. Weak evidence.
agent_relevance: Skilled memory is strategy plus structure, not larger raw capacity. Supports using structured retrieval cues instead of capacity.

source: Jaeggi, Buschkuehl, Jonides, Perrig (2008) Improving fluid intelligence with training on working memory
finding: Founding human claim that dual n-back training raised Gf, with dose dependence. Cited here only as the baseline the LLM papers invoke. Not opened this session.
numbers: Not checked this session; see evidence_a for the numbers.
limits: Not read by this agent.
agent_relevance: Baseline the machine studies are compared to.

source: Melby-Lervag, Redick, Hulme (2016) Working memory training does not improve performance on measures of intelligence or other measures of far transfer
finding: Human meta-analysis finding near transfer but no reliable far transfer. Cited here as the human null against which LLM transfer results are read. Not opened this session.
numbers: Not checked this session; see evidence_a/b.
limits: Not read by this agent.
agent_relevance: Human null result is the reason the project rejects training-style shortcuts.

source: Jaeggi, Buschkuehl, Perrig, Meier (2010) The concurrent validity of the n-back task as a working memory measure
finding: Cited by Zhang 2024 as showing n-back correlates weakly with complex span. Seen only as a citation in Zhang text.
numbers: Not checked; no figure quoted in Zhang's limitation text.
limits: Secondhand via Zhang 2024 limitations section.
agent_relevance: If n-back is a weak WM measure, LLM n-back scores are an even weaker proxy for agent reasoning.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) (U-shaped scaling and code training)
finding: n-back d-prime shows a U-shape over model size. The smallest model copies the input format; larger ones do better. Code-trained text-davinci-002 did well on n-back.
numbers: Smallest model text-ada-001 repeats input format (collapsed responses). Authors link code training in text-davinci-002 to clearer reasoning and lower working-memory load. LLaMA-3 (synthetic data) shows higher d' than LLaMA and LLaMA-2 in their tables.
limits: Causal claims about code and synthetic data are inferred from model-family comparisons, not controlled ablations.
agent_relevance: Training data type (code, step-by-step synthetic) shifts WM-like performance more than n-back practice would. A pretraining effect, outside scaffold control.

source: Synthesis of the n-back debate (Gong 2024 vs Hu and Lewis 2025)
finding: Same paradigm, opposite readings. Gong reads the d' drop at n=3 as a capacity limit near human level. Hu and Lewis show weak models run the wrong task, and Huang 2025 finds no functional hidden memory.
numbers: Gong: GPT-4 above d'=1 at n=1,2,3 (p=9.3e-10 each) and other seven models not. Hu: Llama3.1-70B 0.99/0.93 at 2/3-back, 8B models 0.14/0.17.
limits: Different n-back prompt formats across papers, which changes memory demand.
agent_relevance: Report load effects only after a task-understanding check.

source: Cross-study pattern across Gong 2024, Zhang 2024, Huang 2025, Wang 2025
finding: Across these LLM studies, no practice-style or training-style fix was tested on n-back. Gains came from external scaffolds: CoT, rehearsal text, mock-turn reset, in-context curriculum.
numbers: Examples: CoT lifts Math Magic to 96.7% (o3-mini); mock QA reset lets Gemini Flash 2.0 at 150 updates match 30-45 update baseline; rehearsal prompt +18 points on Object Counting.
limits: My synthesis across papers; none compared scaffolds against weight training on the same task.
agent_relevance: Strong support for the project line: use scaffolds that externalise and reset state. Weight-based transfer (SPIRAL, ViGaL) shows far transfer in models, but it is not available to a prompt-only agent.
